newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet passes 1998 budget, 1997 supplement.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet passes 1998 budget, 1997 supplement.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Friday approved Finance Minister Theo Waigel's 461 billion mark ($263 billion) draft budget for 1998 and a supplementary budget for 1997 that enlarges the deficit, a finance ministry spokeswoman said.

The supplementary budget for this year raises the projected deficit to 71.2 billion marks from an original plan of 53.3 billion, but the government has said it still expects to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU). ($ = 1.753 German Marks)

The cabinet approval sets the stage for parliamentary debate on the bills, expected in special sessions in August or September. Opposition Social Democrats have already attacked the government bills as shaky and lacking in credibility.

Since the 1997 deficit exceeds government investment, the government must now, under the constitution, make a declaration that the excessive deficit is being used to combat an imbalance in the economy.
But that claim has been contested by prominent private economists. The opposition charges the government is not doing enough to fight the main economic problem, record unemployment.
In the 1998 budget, the deficit is seen falling back to 57.8 billion marks.
